summary: Defines a protocol for certificate management between an Internet number resource issuer and a recipient. The recipient can request certificates, revoke them and receive status reports. It is limited to resource certificate management.

eli5.summary: This is the conversation used to ask for, cancel, and check the digital ID cards for internet number blocks, between the one who gives them and the one who gets them.

subtitle: The request and response protocol an address holder uses to get, renew and retire its RPKI resource certificates.

tldr.problem: An organization that has been allocated Internet number resources needs a standard way to ask the issuer for a certificate covering those resources, and to retire keys, so that the issuer's certificates stay aligned with its allocation records.
tldr.mechanism: The subject (client) POSTs a signed XML message over HTTP and the issuer (server) answers with a signed XML message. The messages are list, issue and revoke requests, each with a matching response, plus an error response.
tldr.outcome: The protocol is deliberately limited to resource certificate management and relies on identities and trust set up by other means. Requests run one at a time per client.

facts.label: Retry limit
facts.value: No more than 1 request per 24 hours

today: RFC 6492 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It sits alongside RFC 6480 and RFC 6487 in the RPKI document set.

sections.title: Issuer and Subject
sections.content:
RFC 6492 defines a protocol between an Internet Number Resource issuer and a subject. Resources here means AS numbers, IPv4 addresses and IPv6 addresses. The issuer is a Certification Authority (CA) that issues resource certificates. The subject receives them, and may itself be given a CA-enabled certificate so that it can also act as an issuer.

In the client/server wording of the protocol, the issuer is the server and the subject is the client. A resource class is a collection of resources that can be certified in a single resource certificate by an issuer.

The protocol covers requests for certificate issuance, revocation and status information, and the issuer's allocation database is the authority on what it may certify for a subject. It is intended only for this job and not as part of a more general certificate management framework.
sections.eli5: The one who hands out the number blocks is the server. The one who receives them is the client. A resource class is just one bundle of numbers that goes on one card.

sections.title: What the Protocol Leaves Out
sections.content:
The RFC lists several things it does not cover:

  • signing objects with certified keys, and issuing end-entity certificates;
  • how the issuer's allocation database is consulted, and any protocol for managing the publication repository;
  • how client and server establish identities or exchange the certificates and PKI contexts used for the signed messages;
  • how the two sides reset their local signing time values to mutually recognized values.
sections.eli5: This conversation only handles cards. It does not explain how the two sides first met, or how to post things in the public noticeboard.

sections.title: Transport and the Signed Wrapper
sections.content:
A message exchange starts with the client sending an HTTP POST with content type application/rpki-updown and the message as the body. The server's reply uses the same content type. IANA registered that media type.

Each body is a well-formed CMS signed-data object, DER-encoded, carrying an XML message with content type id-ct-xml (1.2.840.113549.1.9.16.1.28). The profile is strict:

  • there is exactly one signer, and the version fields are 3;
  • exactly one digest algorithm, chosen from the algorithm profile in RFC 6485;
  • the single end-entity (EE) certificate that signed the message MUST be present, together with the current CRL from the CA that issued it;
  • signed attributes MUST include content-type and message-digest, plus signing-time, binary-signing-time or both, and no others; unsigned attributes MUST be omitted.

A recipient must check the structure, verify the signature, validate the EE certificate path to a trust anchor it selected, confirm it is not revoked, and check that the signing time is greater than or equal to that of previously valid messages from the same originator.
sections.eli5: Every message goes in a sealed envelope with the sender's signature and ID. The receiver checks the seal, the ID, and that the date is not older than the last envelope.

sections.title: The Common XML Message
sections.content:
Every message is an XML message element with attributes version (1 in this document), sender, recipient and type. Sender and recipient are names agreed in advance. The type is one of list, list_response, issue, issue_response, revoke, revoke_response or error_response.

Parsers MUST reject documents with a version, element or attribute they do not understand. Servers apply seven checks in order: CMS well-formed, XML well-formed, sender and recipient known, signature valid, certificate valid against the agreed PKI, signing time not older than the last message, and version equal to 1. Errors in these steps MUST produce an HTTP 400 Bad Request, and an error in the version check MUST produce a Request-Not-Performed response. A busy server MAY answer HTTP 503 Service Unavailable, optionally with a Retry-After header.

The protocol is sequential per client. A server MUST NOT accept a new request until it has answered the client's previous one, and parallel requests with the same sender MUST be rejected with error code 1101.
sections.eli5: Each note says who it is from, who it is for, and what kind of note it is. If the server does not understand a note, it says no. And you must wait for the answer before asking again.

sections.title: Listing, Issuing and Revoking
sections.content:
List. The list query has no payload. The list_response contains one class element for each issuer resource class in which the client holds resources. Each has the class name, the URL of the issuer's CA certificate, the AS, IPv4 and IPv6 resource sets, and a resource_set_notafter date. An optional suggested_sia_head names a publication point. It also holds the client's current certificates and the issuer's certificate, Base64 encoded.

Issue. The client sends a request with a class name, optional requested resource sets and a PKCS#10 certificate request. The request is signed with the matching private key as proof of possession. Leaving out all req_resource_set attributes means all resources that match the client's allocation. The client MUST use different key pairs for each resource class. The reply is an issue_response with the issued certificate.

Revoke. A key element with a class name and the ski, a hash of the client's public key, retires that key pair. The server's CA revokes all certificates in that class for this client with that key, and the certificates are withdrawn from the repository and listed in later CRLs. Individual certificates cannot be revoked with this protocol. The reply echoes the same key element.
sections.eli5: List asks, what cards do I hold? Issue says, please make me a card for these numbers and here is my proof it is me. Revoke says, cancel every card made with this key.

sections.title: Errors and Asynchronous Issuance
sections.content:
Any request that cannot be performed gets an error_response carrying a numeric status and an optional human-readable description, where an en-US description must always be included if the element is present. The defined codes range from 1101 to 2001 (see the table).

Some issuers issue certificates through an off-line process. The issuer MUST answer the first request with code 1104, meaning the request is being processed asynchronously, and SHOULD answer repeats with 1101 until done. The client MAY resubmit periodically and SHOULD send no more than 1 request in each 24-hour interval. If a new certificate would be identical to the latest one except for its serial number, the issuer may simply return the latest certificate.
sections.eli5: If the clerk cannot make your card on the spot, they say come back later. You should not keep knocking more than once a day.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The protocol assumes issuer and subject already know each other and have exchanged credentials so they can recognize each other's signatures. How that happens is not described. Strict serialization of each query/response reduces the chance that subject and issuer lose synchronization over the issued certificate state.

Because signing times must not go backwards, a party that sends a valid message with a time in the future forces later messages to carry times at least as large. The signing time need not match a real clock, so large clock skew is allowed. Resetting to an agreed value is outside this protocol.
sections.eli5: Both sides must already trust each other. Because every note must be dated no earlier than the last one, a note dated in the future means later notes must be dated that late too.

viz.caption: THE THREE REQUEST TYPES AND THEIR RESPONSES (ILLUSTRATIVE ORDER, NOT FROM THE RFC)

messages.label: list
messages.note: Which resource classes do I hold?

messages.label: list_response
messages.note: One class element per class with resources.

messages.label: issue
messages.note: Class name plus PKCS#10 certificate request.

messages.label: revoke
messages.note: Class name and SKI of the key to retire.

messages.label: revoke_response
messages.note: Echoes the class name and SKI.

items.label: Already processing request
items.desc: Also used for parallel requests and repeats during off-line issuance.

items.label: Version number error
items.desc: The message version is not understood.

items.label: Unrecognized request type
items.desc: The type attribute is not known.

items.label: No such resource class
items.desc: Issue request names an undefined class.

items.label: No resources allocated in class
items.desc: The client holds nothing in that class.

items.label: Already used key in request
items.desc: Same key pair used for multiple classes.

items.label: Revoke: no such resource class
items.desc: Revoke request names an undefined class.

items.label: Revoke: no such key
items.desc: No certificate matches the given key.
